detached house = a house that is not joined to another house
semi-detached house = a house joined to one other house by a shared wall
block of flats = a tall building with many apartments
cottage = a small house, often in the countryside
attic = the room or space under the roof
basement = a room below the ground floor
chimney = a pipe that takes smoke from a fire out of the house
fence = a barrier around a garden or field
gate = a door in a fence or wall that you can open
driveway = a short private road from the street to a house
wardrobe = a tall cupboard for hanging clothes
chest of drawers = a piece of furniture with drawers for clothes
sink = a bowl with taps where you wash things
tap = the control that water comes out of
dishwasher = a machine that washes plates and cups
central heating = a system that heats all the rooms from one place
neighbour = a person who lives next to you or nearby
outskirts = the areas at the edge of a town or city
city centre = the middle part of a city, with shops and offices
countryside = land that is not a town, with fields and villages
rent = money paid to live in a house you do not own; to pay for this
landlord = the person who owns the house you rent
spacious = having a lot of room inside
cramped = too small and uncomfortable
cosy = warm, comfortable and pleasant
fully furnished = already having beds, tables and other furniture
move house = to leave one home and go to live in another
do the housework = to clean and tidy the home
vacuum cleaner = a machine that sucks up dirt from the floor
curtains = cloth that covers a window
carpet = a thick covering on the floor
balcony = a platform on the outside of a building that you can stand on
downstairs = on a lower floor of the house
upstairs = on a higher floor of the house
suburb = a residential area outside the city centre
hall = the space just inside the front door
flat = a set of rooms on one floor of a building
studio flat = a very small flat that is mainly one room
terraced house = a house in a row that shares walls with neighbours on both sides
bungalow = a house with all the rooms on one floor
skyscraper = a very tall modern building
ground floor = the floor of a building at street level
first floor = the floor above the ground floor (in British English)
lift = a machine that carries people between floors
stairs = a set of steps inside a building
landing = the area at the top of a set of stairs
front door = the main door into a house
back door = a door at the back of a house, often to the garden
doorbell = a button that makes a sound when a visitor arrives
letterbox = the slot in a door for post
roof = the covering on top of a building
garage = a building for keeping a car
garden = land by a house used for plants and sitting outside
lawn = an area of short grass in a garden
hedge = a line of bushes that forms a border
path = a narrow way to walk, for example through a garden
porch = a covered area at the entrance of a house
living room = the main room where a family sits and watches TV
dining room = a room used for eating meals
kitchen = the room where you cook
bedroom = a room with a bed, used for sleeping
bathroom = a room with a bath or shower and usually a toilet
toilet = a bowl you sit on to get rid of waste; a small room for this
study = a room used for reading or working at a desk
utility room = a small room for the washing machine and cleaning tools
sofa = a long, soft seat for two or more people
armchair = a big comfortable chair with sides for your arms
coffee table = a low table in front of a sofa
bookshelf = a board on the wall or a piece of furniture for books
desk = a table for writing or using a computer
lamp = a device that gives light
mirror = a piece of glass that shows your reflection
rug = a small carpet
pillow = a soft cushion for your head in bed
blanket = a large piece of cloth used as a cover on a bed
duvet = a thick bed cover filled with feathers or similar material
sheet = a large piece of cloth on a mattress
mattress = the thick, soft part of a bed that you lie on
bunk beds = two beds, one above the other
shelf = a flat board for putting things on
cupboard = a piece of furniture with doors for storing things
drawer = a box in a piece of furniture that you pull out
washing machine = a machine that washes clothes
tumble dryer = a machine that dries wet clothes
iron = a tool that makes clothes smooth with heat; to use it
radiator = a metal panel on the wall that heats a room
plug = the part that goes into a wall socket; a stopper in a sink
socket = the point in the wall where you connect electricity
light switch = the button on the wall that turns lights on or off
bin = a container for rubbish
recycling bin = a container for paper, glass or plastic that will be reused
doormat = a small rug for wiping shoes at the entrance
key = a small metal object that opens a lock
lock = a device that keeps a door closed until you use a key
alarm = a system that makes a loud noise if someone breaks in
furnished = already containing furniture
unfurnished = without furniture
bills = regular payments for electricity, gas or water
neighbourhood = the area around where you live
residential area = a part of a town with houses rather than factories
village = a small group of houses in the country
town = a place larger than a village but smaller than a city
city = a large, important town
urban = connected with towns and cities
rural = connected with the countryside
noisy = making a lot of loud sound
quiet = with little noise
tidy up = to put things in their places and make a room neat
do the laundry = to wash dirty clothes
hoover = to clean the floor with a vacuum cleaner (British informal)
dust = to wipe away the grey powder that collects on furniture
do the ironing = to make washed clothes smooth with an iron
make the bed = to tidy the covers on a bed after you get up
take the bins out = to carry rubbish containers outside for collection
move in = to start living in a new home
move out = to leave a home and stop living there
share a room = to sleep in the same bedroom as another person
view = what you can see from a window
location = the place where something is
